Title: UCI composition and UL-SCH capacity
TechnicalQuestion: Quantify how HARQ-ACK, CSI Part 1, CSI Part 2, CG-UCI and UTO-UCI consume coded-bit and RE capacity and alter effective UL-SCH code rate.
Baseline: No UCI on an otherwise identical grant.
Treatment: Add one exact UCI composition at a time.
ControlledVariables: Same decoded grant, TB, modulation, rank, channel realization and noise samples.
SweptVariables: OACK, OCSI1, OCSI2, OCGUCI, beta offsets, alpha, one/two codewords.
StatisticalMethod: Exact bit-budget reconciliation; no overlap; decoded UCI equals payload; paired Wilson/McNemar for BLER.
HardAcceptance: At fixed G, added UCI cannot increase GULSCH. Every coded-bit position has exactly one owner.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Measure data-throughput penalty and control-reliability benefit; do not impose a universal BLER direction when TBS adaptation is enabled.

Title: UCI beta-offset sensitivity
TechnicalQuestion: Measure reliability/capacity trade-offs produced by beta-offset and alpha choices.
Baseline: Nominal beta offsets from active configuration.
Treatment: Sweep valid lower and higher beta offsets.
ControlledVariables: Same payload, grant, codeword owner, channel/noise and TB.
StatisticalMethod: Exact Q-prime/E calculation and valid-range checks; invalid values fail before waveform generation.
HardAcceptance: Higher UCI protection must be reflected in exact coded-bit/energy allocation; invalid values create no waveform.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report Pareto frontier between UCI reliability and UL-SCH goodput.

Title: CSI Part 2 payload-size and dependency impact
TechnicalQuestion: Exercise zero, small, boundary and large CSI Part 2 payloads and their dependency on CSI Part 1.
Treatment: Add configured CSI Part 2 payloads.
ControlledVariables: Same report configuration and decoded grant.
SweptVariables: OCSI2, report type, rank, modulation, UCI capacity.
StatisticalMethod: CSI Part 2 without required Part 1 is rejected; exact payload length is never guessed.
HardAcceptance: Payload recovery is bit exact in no-noise tests; insufficient capacity fails with typed error.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify threshold where extra CSI payload materially raises UL-SCH code rate or forces TBS reduction.

Title: UCI-only PUSCH
TechnicalQuestion: Validate PUSCH carrying UCI with zero UL-SCH TB and quantify detection/reliability.
Treatment: TBS=0 with UCI present.
ControlledVariables: Same grant resources and UCI payload.
StatisticalMethod: TBS=0 is handled without fabricated data bits; no-signal false-alarm test included.
HardAcceptance: No-noise UCI recovery is exact; no-signal false decode is below configured bound.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Compare robustness and resource use against mixed data+UCI.

Title: Two-codeword UCI owner selection
TechnicalQuestion: Verify and quantify UCI placement for two UL-SCH transport blocks.
Baseline: One-codeword PUSCH with equivalent total layers.
Treatment: Two codewords with unequal/equal initial I_MCS.
ControlledVariables: Same total rank, channel and total grant.
StatisticalMethod: UCI owner is higher initial I_MCS; tie selects CW0; all owner positions reconcile.
HardAcceptance: Wrong owner injection must be detected by independent position oracle.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify asymmetric codeword impact and whether owner choice changes total goodput.

Title: TBS, base-graph and segmentation boundaries
TechnicalQuestion: Measure discontinuities and correctness at TBS, base-graph, code-block and lifting-size boundaries.
Treatment: Point at and above each boundary.
ControlledVariables: Same resource allocation and target code rate where possible.
SweptVariables: TBS, target code rate, modulation, rank, limited-buffer rate matching.
StatisticalMethod: Pure-spec boundary oracle exactly matches production metadata and bit positions.
HardAcceptance: No off-by-one, negative filler, or unaccounted bit; no-noise TB recovery exact.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Identify performance/complexity steps caused by segmentation changes.

Title: LDPC iterations and LLR scaling
TechnicalQuestion: Quantify decoder complexity and robustness to iteration limit and LLR scaling.
Baseline: Validated nominal LLR scale and iteration limit.
Treatment: Sweep iteration limit and controlled LLR scale errors.
ControlledVariables: Same received samples and rate-recovery output.
StatisticalMethod: No-noise decode must pass at nominal settings; NaN/Inf LLR rejected.
HardAcceptance: Iteration increase cannot change decoded result when CRC already passes; output records convergence.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report complexity/BLER knee; do not tune hidden defaults per operating point.

Title: Decoded DCI ownership and stale-state rejection
TechnicalQuestion: Measure technical consequences of valid versus corrupted/stale scheduling state while enforcing no-waveform behavior for invalid state.
Baseline: CRC-valid DCI 0_x bound to current BWP/RRC epoch.
Treatment: Single-field corruption: CRC, RNTI, BWP, K2, MCS, HARQ, TPMI, epoch.
ControlledVariables: Same underlying intended grant.
StatisticalMethod: Every invalid state creates no waveform and no HARQ mutation.
HardAcceptance: Valid DCI field changes alter actual production resource/coding digest exactly.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Impact is reported as prevented collision/misdecode risk, not as simulated conformance wording.

Title: Configured-grant latency and control overhead
TechnicalQuestion: Compare dynamic scheduling, Type-1 CG and Type-2 CG for periodic and bursty traffic.
Treatment: Configured-grant Type 1 or activated Type 2.
ControlledVariables: Same traffic arrivals, channel, power and resources.
SweptVariables: periodicity, offset, traffic burstiness, activation latency.
StatisticalMethod: CG state machine and exact occasion ownership are hard gates.
HardAcceptance: No transmission outside active occasion; release/activation behavior exact.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify latency/control-overhead benefit and unused-resource cost.

Title: Configured-grant collision, repetition and retransmission
TechnicalQuestion: Analyze collision handling and reliability for CG repetitions and competing dynamic grants.
Treatment: Collision, repetition, dynamic override, retransmission and release cases.
ControlledVariables: Same UE/channel/traffic sequence.
SweptVariables: CG type, repetition count, collision policy, RV sequence.
StatisticalMethod: No double ownership; deterministic policy; HARQ TB identity preserved.
HardAcceptance: Every repeated transmission maps to the correct occasion and RV.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify reliability/latency/resource trade-off.

Title: RAR Msg3 and MsgA uplink coverage
TechnicalQuestion: Validate random-access PUSCH ownership and quantify coverage/power/latency.
Treatment: Pathloss, power ramping, timing error and MsgA variants.
ControlledVariables: Same random-access identity and channel seed.
SweptVariables: RA procedure, pathloss, power ramp step, timing offset.
StatisticalMethod: RAR/MsgA grant fields and identities must be preserved; wrong identity creates no decode.
HardAcceptance: No-noise exact recovery and typed negative cases pass.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify cell-edge access robustness and power cost.

Title: Modulation-order impact
TechnicalQuestion: Compare pi/2-BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM and 256QAM across exact declared profiles.
Treatment: Other supported modulations with valid MCS/TBS.
ControlledVariables: Same rank, grant, channel and power normalization.
StatisticalMethod: Independent constellation and no-noise bit recovery are exact.
HardAcceptance: Unsupported 1024QAM/4096QAM fail before waveform generation in this profile.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Produce SNR gap and spectral-efficiency curves with confidence intervals.

Title: Rank scaling in low-correlation channels
TechnicalQuestion: Measure throughput and reliability from rank 1 through 8 in i.i.d./low-correlation MIMO.
Treatment: Ranks 2-8, valid one/two-codeword mapping.
ControlledVariables: Same total transmit power, bandwidth and channel seeds.
StatisticalMethod: No-noise rank 1-8 exact recovery; power conservation; layer mapping exact.
HardAcceptance: No universal monotonic rank gain is a hard gate; report the rank maximizing goodput.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify multiplexing gain and receiver/complexity cost.

Title: Rank scaling under spatial correlation
TechnicalQuestion: Measure rank collapse and precoder sensitivity as antenna correlation increases.
Treatment: Medium/high correlation with same average path gain.
ControlledVariables: Same rank request, SNR and channel seeds paired by underlying paths.
StatisticalMethod: Channel covariance and applied precoder are exported.
HardAcceptance: No fake rank success through configured SINR; measured per-layer SINR required.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Identify safe rank-selection thresholds.

Title: One- versus two-codeword PUSCH
TechnicalQuestion: Measure coding/decoder and failure asymmetry when ranks 5-8 use two codewords.
Baseline: Equivalent rank with one-codeword profile where valid, or lower-rank matched baseline.
Treatment: Release-valid two-codeword transmission.
ControlledVariables: Same total G, power and channel.
StatisticalMethod: Codeword split and layer mapping exact; TB identities independent.
HardAcceptance: No codeword may be silently dropped or duplicated.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify unequal-MCS and unequal-channel impact per codeword.

Title: Codebook versus non-codebook transmission
TechnicalQuestion: Compare SRS-driven codebook and non-codebook PUSCH under matched channel information.
Treatment: Non-codebook transmission using valid SRS resource indicators.
ControlledVariables: Same channel, rank, power and SRS observation.
StatisticalMethod: Applied matrix digest must originate from measured SRS decision and match TX.
HardAcceptance: Stale/mismatched SRS creates no strict transmission when required.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify robustness and overhead differences.

Title: DM-RS additional positions versus Doppler
TechnicalQuestion: Measure channel-tracking benefit and RE overhead of additional DM-RS positions.
Treatment: Higher additional-position configurations.
ControlledVariables: Same mapping type, rank, ports, channel paths and SNR.
StatisticalMethod: DM-RS positions/ports exactly match independent table vectors.
HardAcceptance: No-noise recovery exact for every valid tuple.
DiagnosticInterpretation: At high Doppler, report NMSE/BLER improvement versus overhead; direction is statistical.

Title: DM-RS configuration type versus delay spread
TechnicalQuestion: Compare configuration type 1 and 2 under frequency selectivity.
Treatment: Type 2 where valid.
ControlledVariables: Same channel realization, rank, total power and symbol positions.
SweptVariables: delay profile, RMS delay spread, config type.
StatisticalMethod: Exact RE/port/OCC mapping; no port overwrite.
HardAcceptance: Invalid type/rank/port combinations fail before waveform.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify frequency-domain estimation trade-off.

Title: DM-RS length, OCC and high-rank port support
TechnicalQuestion: Exercise length-1/2 DM-RS, OCC and logical ports for high-rank PUSCH.
Treatment: Length 2 and ranks/ports up to 8 where valid.
ControlledVariables: Same channel and resource allocation.
SweptVariables: DMRSLength, CDM groups, port set, rank.
StatisticalMethod: Requested and applied logical port sets must be identical and valid.
HardAcceptance: Cross-port correlation meets independent sequence/OCC expectations.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify high-rank estimation robustness and overhead.

Title: DM-RS port orthogonality and leakage
TechnicalQuestion: Directly measure inter-port leakage under ideal and impaired synchronization.
Treatment: Controlled timing/CFO and multi-UE shared-resource cases.
ControlledVariables: Same DM-RS sequences and power.
SweptVariables: port pairs, CFO, timing offset, UE identities.
StatisticalMethod: Ideal independent vectors must match exact correlations.
HardAcceptance: Wrong port/identity must not decode another UE payload.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify orthogonality loss with impairments.

Title: PT-RS density versus phase noise
TechnicalQuestion: Measure CPE tracking, EVM and BLER for valid PT-RS densities under phase noise.
Treatment: Valid time/frequency density and port association.
ControlledVariables: Same phase-noise realization and received samples.
StatisticalMethod: Exact PT-RS indices/sequence/port association; before/after CPE recorded.
HardAcceptance: Under selected nonzero phase-noise stress, correction must reduce paired CPE RMSE and EVM.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify overhead versus robustness and optimum density.

Title: PT-RS overhead with negligible phase noise
TechnicalQuestion: Measure whether unnecessary PT-RS reduces data capacity without receiver benefit.
Treatment: PT-RS enabled, phase noise off.
ControlledVariables: Same grant, TB adaptation policy and noise samples.
StatisticalMethod: CPE estimate remains near zero; exact overhead accounting.
HardAcceptance: No claim that PT-RS always improves performance.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report pure overhead and any estimation noise penalty.

Title: CP-OFDM versus DFT-s-OFDM PAPR
TechnicalQuestion: Quantify PAPR and spectral behavior of exact single-layer transform precoding.
Treatment: Transform precoding enabled for valid single-layer tuples.
ControlledVariables: Same data symbols, allocation and total energy.
StatisticalMethod: Unitary DFT energy and no-noise round trip are exact.
HardAcceptance: Multi-layer transform precoding is rejected.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report PAPR distribution; selected configurations should show expected DFT-s-OFDM reduction without hardcoding a universal dB gain.

Title: Transform precoding under PA backoff/clipping
TechnicalQuestion: Measure how lower PAPR changes EVM/BLER at finite PA backoff.
Baseline: CP-OFDM through the same normalized PA model.
Treatment: DFT-s-OFDM through the same PA model.
ControlledVariables: Same input average power, symbols, channel and noise.
SweptVariables: PA backoff, clipping level, modulation, NPRB.
StatisticalMethod: PA model and scaling reference points identical; linear-PA baseline reconciles.
HardAcceptance: No-noise linear PA gives identical decoded bits.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify backoff saving and nonlinear robustness.

Title: Frequency hopping null test in AWGN
TechnicalQuestion: Prove that hopping only remaps resources and does not create artificial gain in flat AWGN.
Treatment: Intra-slot or inter-slot hopping.
ControlledVariables: Same total resources, data, noise samples and channel gain.
StatisticalMethod: Exact hop maps match independent oracle; paired performance difference is within numerical/statistical tolerance.
HardAcceptance: Any large AWGN gain indicates scaling or noise inconsistency.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Use as a null experiment before diversity claims.

Title: Frequency-hopping diversity in selective fading
TechnicalQuestion: Quantify frequency diversity under TDL/CDL channels.
Treatment: Intra-slot/inter-slot hopping.
ControlledVariables: Paired channel paths/noise and same total resources.
SweptVariables: delay profile, hop offset, allocation width, SNR.
StatisticalMethod: Hop-specific DM-RS/PT-RS and receiver extraction exact.
HardAcceptance: Performance effects use paired confidence intervals, not single-seed curves.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report when hopping helps, is neutral, or hurts due to estimation/overhead.

Title: Hopping, repetition and HARQ interaction
TechnicalQuestion: Analyze whether repeated transmissions sample independent frequency regions and combine correctly.
Treatment: Repetition/HARQ with valid hopping.
ControlledVariables: Same TB identity, RV sequence and channel process.
SweptVariables: repetition type/count, hop mode, RV sequence.
StatisticalMethod: Each retransmission’s bit positions and resource digest are preserved.
HardAcceptance: Combining never mixes different TB identities or codeword layouts.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify latency/reliability gain.

Title: SRS SNR versus RI/SRI/TPMI accuracy
TechnicalQuestion: Measure decision accuracy and PUSCH loss as SRS quality varies.
Treatment: Measured SRS at swept SNR.
ControlledVariables: Same underlying channel and candidate codebook.
SweptVariables: SRS SNR, rank, codebook, antenna count.
StatisticalMethod: Decision and application digests match; configured TPMI fallback forbidden in strict path.
HardAcceptance: Stale/undetected SRS is explicit, not replaced by ideal CSI.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Generate accuracy and downstream BLER curves.
Dependencies: SRS estimator and PUSCH decision object

Title: SRS age versus mobility
TechnicalQuestion: Quantify precoder aging at different Doppler/mobility.
Treatment: Reuse decision after increasing age.
ControlledVariables: Same channel trajectory and noise seed.
StatisticalMethod: Age and configuration epoch exported; hard max-age enforced.
HardAcceptance: Decisions beyond validity create no strict transmission or trigger re-sounding policy.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Estimate safe sounding periodicity.

Title: SRS bandwidth/resource coverage impact
TechnicalQuestion: Measure precoding and link-adaptation loss when SRS samples only part of the scheduled PUSCH band.
Treatment: Partial-band/narrow sounding with valid association.
ControlledVariables: Same channel and PUSCH allocation.
SweptVariables: SRS bandwidth, comb, hopping, PUSCH bandwidth.
StatisticalMethod: Coverage and association are exact and exported.
HardAcceptance: No full-band claim from partial-band observations.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify bandwidth/overhead versus accuracy.

Title: Perfect CSI, measured SRS and stale/configured precoder comparison
TechnicalQuestion: Create a bounded upper/lower benchmark for precoding.
Treatment: Fresh measured SRS, stale SRS and fixed configured matrix.
ControlledVariables: Same channel/noise and TX power.
StatisticalMethod: Only perfect CSI is labelled oracle; fixed configured matrix is an ablation, never strict evidence.
HardAcceptance: Applied source and digest recorded.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Measure implementation gap to oracle and harm from shortcuts.

Title: Reciprocity/calibration-error sensitivity
TechnicalQuestion: Measure impact of UL antenna-chain calibration error on SRS-derived precoding.
Treatment: Amplitude/phase calibration errors.
ControlledVariables: Same propagation channel and SRS noise.
SweptVariables: phase error, gain error, antenna count.
StatisticalMethod: Calibration error is an explicit impairment with provenance.
HardAcceptance: No hidden ideal reciprocity when impairment enabled.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify calibration accuracy requirement.

Title: Open-loop PUSCH power-control impact
TechnicalQuestion: Verify exact power equation and pathloss compensation across bandwidth/numerology/pathloss.
Treatment: Sweep P0, alpha, M_PUSCH, numerology and pathloss.
ControlledVariables: Same waveform symbols and channel pathloss.
SweptVariables: P0, alpha, pathloss, mu, MRB, DeltaTF.
StatisticalMethod: Independent power equation matches before clipping and actual waveform RMS power.
HardAcceptance: Configured SNR cannot substitute for measured pathloss.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify cell-center/edge power and BLER.

Title: Closed-loop TPC convergence
TechnicalQuestion: Measure convergence and stability of accumulated/absolute TPC loops.
Treatment: Closed-loop TPC with known command sequence and gNB target error.
ControlledVariables: Same pathloss trajectory and waveform.
SweptVariables: TPC mode, command delay, step sequence, measurement noise.
StatisticalMethod: State transition matches independent recurrence exactly.
HardAcceptance: No per-point reset or hidden clipping except P_CMAX.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report stability and convergence speed.

Title: P_CMAX clipping and saturation
TechnicalQuestion: Quantify cell-edge behavior when requested power exceeds UE limit.
Treatment: Pathloss/PRB/rank causing P_CMAX clipping.
ControlledVariables: Same P0/alpha and target received power.
StatisticalMethod: Applied power equals min(requested, P_CMAX) with exact waveform reconciliation.
HardAcceptance: TPC state must not fabricate achieved power.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Show coverage loss and saturation region.

Title: Pathloss-measurement noise in power control
TechnicalQuestion: Measure sensitivity to noisy/stale reference-signal pathloss estimates.
Treatment: Noisy or aged pathloss estimate.
ControlledVariables: Same actual pathloss trajectory.
StatisticalMethod: Estimate provenance/age exported; configured SNR fallback forbidden.
HardAcceptance: Filter behavior deterministic for fixed observations.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify required measurement quality.

Title: Near-far and inter-cell power externality
TechnicalQuestion: Analyze whether power control balances desired reception without excessive interference.
Treatment: Near/far UEs and inter-cell interferer.
ControlledVariables: Same traffic and scheduler allocation.
SweptVariables: pathloss imbalance, alpha, TPC target, power cap.
StatisticalMethod: Per-UE waveform powers and channel gains independently reconciled.
HardAcceptance: No shared scalar noise/interference shortcut.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify fairness and interference trade-off.

Title: ZF, MMSE and IRC receiver impact
TechnicalQuestion: Compare receiver algorithms under noise, spatial correlation and interference.
Treatment: ZF and IRC with valid covariance.
ControlledVariables: Same received grid/channel estimate/noise samples.
StatisticalMethod: IRC requires finite PSD covariance and may not silently fall back.
HardAcceptance: No-interference IRC/MMSE equivalence is a null check; ZF instability is reported.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify receiver gain and complexity.

Title: Interference-covariance quality and age
TechnicalQuestion: Measure IRC degradation from stale, undersampled or biased covariance.
Treatment: Aged, low-sample or mismatched covariance.
ControlledVariables: Same received waveform.
SweptVariables: age, sample count, diagonal loading, mismatch.
StatisticalMethod: Invalid covariance is rejected; no MMSE fallback in strict IRC.
HardAcceptance: Covariance source, sample count and age recorded.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Determine minimum covariance quality.

Title: HARQ RV and soft-combining gain
TechnicalQuestion: Verify bit-position-aware combining and quantify reliability over RV sequences.
Treatment: RV sequences such as 0-2-3-1 with exact rate recovery.
ControlledVariables: Same TB identity, channel process and noise seeds.
StatisticalMethod: Independent rate-matching positions match; no combining across TB/layout mismatch.
HardAcceptance: No-noise retransmission identity exact; injected wrong RV detected.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify reliability and latency gain.

Title: HARQ latency-throughput trade-off
TechnicalQuestion: Measure retransmission budget, deadline misses and goodput.
Treatment: 1-3 allowed retransmissions with selected RV policy.
ControlledVariables: Same arrivals, channel traces and scheduler resources.
StatisticalMethod: HARQ timing and process ownership exact.
HardAcceptance: No duplicate delivery after late success.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Identify operating point for reliability versus latency.

Title: Two-UE MU-PUSCH on shared PRBs
TechnicalQuestion: Validate UE identity separation, DM-RS orthogonality, covariance and multi-user detection.
Treatment: Shared PRBs with valid separate DM-RS resources and spatial channels.
ControlledVariables: Same total bandwidth and per-UE offered load.
SweptVariables: power imbalance, spatial correlation, rank, receiver.
StatisticalMethod: Wrong UE/DM-RS identity does not decode; per-UE resource/power ledger exact.
HardAcceptance: No oracle separation labels in receiver.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify MU gain and degradation regions.

Title: Receiver-measured SINR calibration
TechnicalQuestion: Validate reported post-equalization SINR against analytical AWGN and empirical EVM/BLER.
Baseline: Analytical AWGN SNR at receiver reference point.
Treatment: Receiver-derived per-layer SINR.
ControlledVariables: Same waveform/noise realization and known channel.
StatisticalMethod: Every strict result has finite receiver-derived SINR and sample count.
HardAcceptance: Removing measured SINR must fail the run.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify estimator bias across channels and receivers.

Title: No-signal, wrong-identity and false-decode robustness
TechnicalQuestion: Measure false alarm and reject behavior for absent or mismatched PUSCH.
Treatment: No signal, wrong RNTI/scrambling ID, wrong DM-RS port, wrong slot, wrong BWP.
ControlledVariables: Same receiver search space and noise.
StatisticalMethod: Invalid assignment generates no TX; no-signal false-decoding campaign meets configured bound.
HardAcceptance: Receiver never uses transmitted bits or oracle indices not available in procedure.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify detection integrity.

Title: CFO sensitivity
TechnicalQuestion: Measure timing/channel/phase tracking under carrier-frequency offset.
Treatment: Swept CFO normalized by SCS.
ControlledVariables: Same channel, noise, synchronization policy.
SweptVariables: CFO Hz, SCS, PTRS state, modulation.
StatisticalMethod: CFO is applied in waveform time domain and receiver estimate has provenance.
HardAcceptance: No hidden perfect correction unless oracle profile.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report tolerable CFO and PT-RS interaction.

Title: Timing-offset sensitivity
TechnicalQuestion: Measure acquisition and residual timing error effects.
Treatment: Offsets within/outside CP and residual estimator errors.
ControlledVariables: Same channel/noise and synchronization method.
StatisticalMethod: Offset is applied to waveform; receiver may not consume true offset in strict mode.
HardAcceptance: No-noise within-CP cases recover after valid estimation.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify timing margin.

Title: Phase-noise and PT-RS interaction across SCS
TechnicalQuestion: Measure phase-noise robustness jointly over SCS, modulation and PT-RS density.
Treatment: Phase noise with PT-RS off/on and density sweep.
ControlledVariables: Same oscillator realization scaled per profile.
StatisticalMethod: Phase-noise model and PT-RS correction reference points explicit.
HardAcceptance: Selected stress cases must show paired CPE/EVM improvement with valid PT-RS.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Build operating-region map.

Title: Numerology and mobility interaction
TechnicalQuestion: Measure PUSCH performance as SCS and Doppler change.
Treatment: 15/60/120 kHz valid profiles and mobility sweep.
ControlledVariables: Matched occupied bandwidth and channel path powers where feasible.
SweptVariables: SCS, Doppler, DMRS density, PTRS, hopping.
StatisticalMethod: Uses canonical frame/grid engine; no local numerology assumptions.
HardAcceptance: All selected tuples pass no-noise mapping first.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Quantify robustness/latency/overhead trade-offs.

Title: Runtime and memory scaling
TechnicalQuestion: Measure computational cost of exact implementation.
Treatment: Sweep PRBs, rank, codewords, UCI load, receiver and LDPC iterations.
ControlledVariables: Same hardware/toolchain, warm-up and measurement protocol.
StatisticalMethod: Timing excludes first-run JIT warm-up and records MATLAB/toolbox version.
HardAcceptance: No performance pass/fail hides functional failure.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Identify bottlenecks and regression thresholds.

Title: Seed sensitivity and reproducibility
TechnicalQuestion: Prove deterministic replay and quantify uncertainty across random seeds.
Treatment: Independent seed set.
ControlledVariables: Identical configuration and toolchain.
SweptVariables: seed, parallel/serial execution, channel/noise RNG stream.
StatisticalMethod: Same-seed raw artifacts and metrics must match exactly within documented floating tolerance.
HardAcceptance: Parallel merge order cannot change counts or random streams.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Report required seed count for stable conclusions.

Title: Feature-interaction factorial study
TechnicalQuestion: Detect interactions among UCI load, DM-RS density, PT-RS, transform precoding and hopping.
Baseline: All selected features off/minimal where valid.
Treatment: 2-level fractional/full factorial combinations.
ControlledVariables: Same base grant, channel paths and paired seeds.
SweptVariables: UCI, DMRS, PTRS, transform precoding, hopping, phase noise, Doppler.
StatisticalMethod: Every combination is validated for normative compatibility before run.
HardAcceptance: Invalid combinations are negative tests, not silently altered.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Fit main effects and two-way interactions with confidence intervals.

Title: End-to-end technical deployment scenarios
TechnicalQuestion: Exercise coherent PUSCH profiles rather than isolated kernels.
Treatment: Cell-center, cell-edge, high-mobility, phase-noise, high-rank, CG and MU profiles.
ControlledVariables: Pinned scenario definitions and seed lists.
StatisticalMethod: All profile prerequisites pass and every metric is production-derived.
HardAcceptance: No aggregate pass if a required scenario is blocked or incomplete.
DiagnosticInterpretation: Provide final technical capability/impact summary without marketing claims.
